e.text: A2 hit 17.2% vs benchmark 3.9%; asking the Critic how to push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A2, A3

critique.summary: A2 is the strongest plan: two early host-read podcast ads plus targeted city social reach 17.2% (P10 16.2%) at $5.91 per adopter, against 3.9% for the benchmark, and podcasts and social drive most adoption. The $300 zone partners and A3's day-25 El Tio Carnitas pop-up add few adopters for their cost, and the pop-up comes too late for word of mouth to spread.

findings.finding: Reaches 17.2% (P10 16.2%) with 2512 adopters at $5.91 each; Bodega Boys (257 for $3450) and The Brilliant Idiots (226 for $3450) are close to the social ads (352 for $5040), while the three $300 partners add only 4–8 each.
Swapping the second podcast for $1800 of partners and a $2500 pop-up drops reach to 13.2% (P10 12.5%), 582 fewer adopters than A2, at $7.66 each.
The El Tio Carnitas pop-up in Lynwood on day 25 is credited with 13 adopters for $2500 (about $192 each), and the Latin music and gaming district comes in lowest at 11.4%.
Spends $10240 for 3.9% reach and 568 adopters ($18.03 each); its street teams get 0–1 adopters per $450.

changes.change: Keep A2's day-0 Bodega Boys and day-2 Brilliant Idiots reads and city social for days 0–28, and cut the three weakest partners: Krab Queenz in Hyde Park (4), Fun-Diggity Funnel-Cakes in Willowbrook (6) and James Fishmarket in Willowbrook (8).
changes.why: These $300 partners add only 4–8 adopters each, while the podcasts return about 70 adopters per $1000.

changes.change: Do not use a launch pop-up on day 25 (as at El Tio Carnitas in Lynwood). If a pop-up is tested, schedule it by day 3–5 in Gardena (fit 0.823) or Willowbrook (0.815).
changes.why: The day-25 pop-up got 13 adopters for $2500, leaving no time for word of mouth, which makes up 49–54% of adoption.

changes.change: Test adding the Fear of God drop alongside A2's Stüssy drop, funded by the $900 from the cut partners plus the $160 left in the budget, or else swap Stüssy for Fear of God.
changes.why: Fear of God (152) and Stüssy (157) each return about 76 adopters per $2000, far more than the partners.

e.note: A2 is the strongest plan: two early host-read podcast ads plus targeted city social reach 17.2% (P10 16.2%) at $5.91 per adopter, against 3.9% for the benchmark, and podcasts and social drive most adoption. The $300 zone partners and A3's day-25 El Tio Carnitas pop-up add few adopters for their cost, and the pop-up comes too late for word of mouth to spread.

e.text: Applying the Critic's notes: cut weak partners, test a third podcast or Fear of God drop.

e.note: Revising: Keep A2 core (Bodega Boys day 0, Brilliant Idiots day 2, city social, Stüssy). Cut the $300 partners. Revision 1: add Fear of God drop. Revision 2: add a third early podcast read (The Read or Drink Champs) instead. Stay under $15,000.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for A2

plan.headline: Album Release Show at the Wiltern: podcast-led launch projected to reach ~17% of LA's natural audience (~2,500 fans) for $14,840
plan.summary: The bet is to front-load host-read ads on Bodega Boys and The Brilliant Idiots, backed by a 28-day Stüssy drop and city-wide targeted social, because this audience is spread across LA rather than packed into a few hot spots. Qloo taste data shows this crowd over-indexes on both shows (0.98 and 0.96) and on Stüssy (0.96), pulled in by Kendrick Lamar, ScHoolboy Q and SZA. The simulation projects 17.2% reach (16.2%–18.1%), about 2,512 adopters at $5.91 each, with more than half coming from word of mouth, versus 3.9% for a crowd-chasing benchmark; this is a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.

Day 2 (25 days out): The Brilliant Idiots host-read ad goes live ($3,450)

risks: All projections come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data; real reach could fall outside the 16.2%–18.1% range.
Word of mouth drives 53.9% of simulated adoption; if sharing is weaker in real life, results drop sharply.
The three restaurant partners drove only 4–8 simulated adopters each, so their value is mostly local presence.
Simulated fans like Diego flagged the trek to Koreatown on a weeknight as a barrier, which the plan does not address.
